prompt:
Use case: photorealistic-natural. Rework the supplied previous hero image into a substantially more immersive, refined Japanese knitting-room editorial photograph. Landscape 3:2, highest resolution available, ideally 3072x2048. This must feel like an inhabited room photographed with a full-frame 50mm lens at f/4, not a studio still life.

Reference roles: r1/d2.png is the previous composition to improve, NOT the quality target. ref/site_wide.png and ref/room_desktop.png establish the cream plaster, old honey oak and tactile inviting interior. The two s2 product photographs are authoritative for yarn identity: use ONLY the green/yellow/cream colorway, bottom-right of the swatch grid. Preserve its fresh yellow-green, moss, deeper muted forest green, golden yellow, creamy white, long airy fine fiber halo and loosely cross-wound oblong pull-skein shape. No cake rolls, no round uniform balls, no boucle. Do not copy packaging, words, trays or baskets. Logo reference is for terracotta #AB5631 ONLY; render no logo.

LAYOUT IS MANDATORY: Left 55% of canvas is uninterrupted softly and evenly illuminated cream plaster wall until a shallow floor strip at y=87%. Full top 14% stays quiet blank cream. Keep ALL furniture, yarn, scarf, props, curtain and architectural corners to the right of x=56% and below y=16%. The table's leftmost edge begins at x=57%, y=65%; do not expand the table across the text area. Subject and complete fringe fit at x=64–90%, y=57–94%. Leave breathing room below fringe.

Create convincing depth entirely in the right half: a cream wall return at x=87% reveals a recessed window nook; a narrow softly lit natural linen curtain edge begins below the top safe band at far right. A low aged oak open shelf at x=79–98%, y=28–53%, visibly well BEHIND the table with space between them, holds a small naturally irregular assortment of unlabelled neutral wool skeins, softly out of focus. No tall shelf. Shelf perspective, wall reveal, ambient shadow and occlusion should convey several feet of room depth. One small matte terracotta pottery vessel on that rear shelf. No plants or baskets.

Soft but directional real afternoon window light comes from off-frame left, casting believable graduated shadows and textured light across the RIGHT-side tabletop and lower floor only. The left copy wall remains low contrast and uncluttered, no hard window grids across it. Rich but restrained tonal depth, neutral cream highlights, nuanced shadows, no orange filter. Small worn patches in old oak, a subtle old cup ring, rubbed table edge and slightly uneven jute rug edge suggest use, not artificial distressed repeated dots. A relaxed small fold of terracotta linen on the far-right tabletop under a simple butter-yellow ceramic tea cup introduces brand color quietly, never competes with green yarn. Only these minimal useful props and knitting tools.

Hero textile: a half-knitted narrow fringed scarf made from the exact referenced fuzzy space-dyed yarn, draped over table edge. Authentic continuous knitted V stitches softly veiled by fine irregular long fibers, airy and supple rather than chunky, felted or plastic. Irregular-width horizontal bands and nuanced transition stitches of forest green, yellow-green, moss, golden yellow and cream. No perfectly repeated stripe formula. Finished lower cast-on edge with a modest number of believable hand-knotted fringe bundles, fully visible. Unfinished upper edge on tabletop, every live loop threaded on ONE straight wooden needle, realistic scale and perspective. ONE continuous working strand clearly runs from the endmost live stitch to the working skein beside it, rests naturally on the table, with no branch or disconnected tail. A second complete straight matching wooden needle rests separately nearby without impossible intersections.

EXACTLY THREE product skeins on the foreground table: one working skein at x=83%, y=58%, golden-yellow/cream with green wraps, two extra same-product skeins at x=91%, y=52% and x=95%, y=63%, varied angles and winding stages, naturally oblong, distinct not cloned. All foreground skeins match the real product's fuzzy fine strands and loose crisscross winding. No perfectly front-facing display. Background shelf skeins are clearly separate, subdued and out of focus.

Avoid text, numbers, labels, paper bands, packaging, logos, UI, humans or animals. Avoid glowing fibers, floating particles, false halos, fake blur, excessive haze, oversharpening, overly clean showroom surfaces, distorted needles, disconnected yarn, knitted crochet stitches or repeated synthetic wood grain. Real physically grounded contact shadows. The result should retain usable safe space but feel as spatially rich and inviting as the site reference.
FINAL REVISION after reviewing the first generated result: Its table starts at x=41%, which is unacceptable. Recompose, not just restyle. Move and scale the ENTIRE right-side furniture and still-life assembly so its LEFTMOST pixel starts at x=56%. Scarf must be entirely within x=66–88%, fringe bottom y=92%. Keep the three foreground skeins fully within the frame. The full rectangle x=0–55%, y=0–86% is plain low-contrast cream wall without sun patches or diagonal shadows. The full rectangle x=0–100%, y=0–14% is quiet cream wall: no curtain, window, corner line or objects in this band. Curtain/window nook may appear ONLY below y=16% on far right, like a recessed lower window with its upper boundary outside the visible opening. Preserve convincing shelf depth, terracotta pottery and linen, butter-yellow cup, natural fibers and gentle window lighting on right-side objects and bottom floor. Pull back enough that composition truly meets these measured boundaries.
Final targeted edit (applied to the intermediate generated image):
Edit the supplied image. Preserve the photographic room, exact green/yellow/cream fuzzy yarn, three tabletop skeins, scarf, shelf and pottery. Make these mandatory layout changes: (1) Reduce and shift the complete table and all its contents to the right so absolutely no table or scarf exists left of 56% image width. Table corner should be at pixel x=880 on this 1536-wide image. (2) Remove the curtain and window entirely, replacing them with cream plaster wall. The room corner line must fade out before reaching the top 150 pixels. Entire top 150 pixels is plain cream wall. (3) Raise floor-wall boundary to no higher than y=880 on 1024-height image; left wall extends to that height. Keep natural window illumination coming from OFF CAMERA, with sunlight only on floor and right table. Preserve depth through the low shelf, spatial separation and shadows. Complete fringe visible above bottom edge. No writing or labels. Photorealistic 3:2. This is a precise composition repair; retain beautiful product textures and terracotta accents.
